title: Wallpaper Groups — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Wallpaper Groups' rich face, its first round at Sketch tier: three made pieces that each walk up to a test the page's own text sets (which turns a lattice can hold and how the seventeen really split, one tile put through all seventeen against the kaleidoscope sentence, and a two-voice loop put to the rhythmic impossibility sentence), and the May p4m cell laid beside the Alhambra, with the fingerprint of the words each was laid against and the offers the pieces measured for the text. I grow when a piece has something new to test; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The list's counts are wrong for its labels. Counted on the which-turns piece's engine, the section's own four kinds hold 1 (p1), 3 (pm, pg, cm), 4 (p2, p3, p4, p6) and 9 (pmm, pmg, pgg, cmm, p4m, p4g, p3m1, p31m, p6m), not 4, 5, 3, 5; read with glides as reflections, the only reading that fills all four bins. The section's numbers are the split by highest turn, 4, 5, 3, then 3 + 2, under other names. Proposed: "1 with translation only (p1); 3 with reflection or glide and no turn (pm, pg, cm); 4 with turns and no reflection (p2, p3, p4, p6); 9 that mix turns with mirrors or glides." Or keep four lines and split by turn: none 4, half 5, third 3, quarter 3, sixth 2.

"Rotate the central fragment, and the entire pattern rotates in lockstep" holds only in the 5 groups with no reflection (p1, p2, p3, p4, p6). Measured on the one-tile piece's engine: turn the tile 0.3 rad and every unreflected copy turns +0.3, every reflected copy −0.3, in all 12 groups with a mirror or glide, exactly half the copies each; and no copy's centre moves, so the pattern as a whole never turns. A kaleidoscope is made of mirrors (three in a triangle give p3m1, p4m or p6m), so it is one of the 12. Proposed: "Turn the central fragment and every copy turns with it, the mirrored ones the other way: the pattern changes, and its symmetry holds."

"In 1985, crystallographer M.C. Escher and mathematician H.S.M. Coxeter established … all 17" doesn't stand. Escher was a graphic artist, not a crystallographer, and died in 1972; he visited the Alhambra in 1922 and 1936 and copied its tilings, and he and Coxeter corresponded from 1954, but no source found has either counting its groups. The record: Edith Müller's 1944 Zürich thesis found 12 (Grünbaum's reading; Bodner reads 11); Grünbaum, Grünbaum and Shephard (1986) found at most 13, missing p2, pg, pgg and p3m1; Pérez-Gómez and Montesinos (1987) reported all 17; Grünbaum disputed that count in Notices of the AMS (June/July 2006), noting the count changed with what was counted (colours, interlace, a single tile); Bodner (Bridges 2013) located 14, missing p2, pmg and p3m1. Proposed: "Whether all 17 are there is still argued: Müller counted 12 in 1944, Montesinos claimed all 17 in 1987, Grünbaum disputed it in 2006, and Bodner found 14 in 2013." The section's "Not mostly. Not about. All 17.", its next paragraph, and the forward vector's "encoded all 17" lean on the contested count. Sources: Grünbaum, faculty.washington.edu/moishe/branko/BG262.Alhambra.pdf; Bodner, sites.uwm.edu/ancel/files/2017/04/Bodner.Planar-Crystallographic-Groups-Represtented-at-the-Alhambra.2013-xsue3q.pdf.

offers.section: Musical Symmetry: Rhythm as Wallpaper Group
offers.what: The rhythmic impossibility sentence holds in a 16-step bar and fails in other loops. Measured on the rhythm piece's engine: in 16 steps a fifth of a turn is 3.2 steps, and five cells of 3 leave a 1-step gap, five of 4 overlap by 4, neither five-fold; in 15 steps (cells of 3) or 20 (cells of 4) there is no gap, no overlap, and the loop is five-fold. Every k from 2 to 12 fits a loop of 2k steps. On a timeline a turn of the loop is a slide in time, and the limit is that k divides the loop's length: arithmetic, not geometry, and no turn is forbidden outright. Proposed: "The crystallographic restriction has a musical shadow, but a softer one: a loop can be five-fold only if five divides its length. A 16-step bar can't hold it; a 15- or 20-step loop can."

offers.section: Musical Symmetry: Rhythm as Wallpaper Group
offers.what: A repeating rhythm is a strip, not a plane: time runs along it, the voices across it, and it repeats in one direction only. Its symmetries are the 7 frieze groups, not the 17 wallpaper groups; random two-voice loops on the rhythm piece's engine reach exactly the seven (p1, p11g, p11m, p1m1, p2, p2mg, p2mm). On one voice, a half-turn and a mirror in time make the same loop (all 256 first halves of a 16-step loop). The glide is also misplaced: kick-snare-kick-snare is itself p2mg, its glide one beat along with low and high swapped; the section puts the glide in the quarter-note hi-hat instead. Proposed: "A repeating rhythm is a frieze group in time, one of seven …" with the glide example moved to the kick-snare.

offers.section: Musical Symmetry: Rhythm as Wallpaper Group
offers.what: Aimed at the bundle's recipe-p2, recorded here because the rhythm piece measured it: its rule, "a hit at position n maps to position (n + 8) mod 16", is a slide, not a 180° turn. On a cell with no symmetry of its own it makes p1 (hop), with no half-turn. On one line a true half-turn is the reversal n → 17 − n, which is recipe-pm's mirror; p2 and pm come apart only with a second voice (the piece's two-voice step: half-turn reverses and swaps the voices, making p2).

offers.section: Wallpaper Groups in World Music — An Initial Mapping
offers.what: The Ewe bell is named E(5,12) but its accents, 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, are seven: checked on the rhythm piece's engine, the list is E(7,12) turned (Toussaint's standard bell), not E(5,12). The same check finds the listed pattern doesn't land on itself under a third of a turn (4 steps), so it has no three-fold skeleton of its own; the "is p3" line may want a second look when the section is next worked.

Seen in passing, not tested by a piece: "the Shubnikov groups (double groups)". Shubnikov groups are the black-and-white (antisymmetry, magnetic) groups, where an operation may swap two colours; double groups are a different construction, for half-integer spin. The parenthesis wants dropping or replacing with "black-and-white groups". The bullet's "color-preserving operations" also fights its own "anti-symmetries where color reverses".

pieces.title: which turns fit · five steps
pieces.caption: **Which turns can a repeating pattern hold?** A square lattice turned until its points land, then any turn on square and hexagonal lattices, then the fifth-turn: pentagons leave 36° or overlap 72°, and a set closed under a fifth-turn has no shortest step (0.382, 0.236, 0.146, each the golden ratio smaller). The test: 2·cos(360°/n) must be whole, so n is 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6. Last, the seventeen from one tile, sorted. By the section's own kinds they count 1, 3, 4, 9, not 4, 5, 3, 5; the section's numbers are the split by highest turn. Checked in Node on the piece's own engine.

pieces.title: one p4m cell · the May 2026 proofs
pieces.caption: One p4m cell: eight copies of one comma about a square, four-fold centres on the mirrors. Bodner (2013) photographs a p4m tile dado in the Mirador de Lindaraja. The sheet's own line calls p4m the most symmetric group; p6m is, with twelve copies to p4m's eight.

pieces.title: rhythm on a strip · five steps
pieces.caption: **Rhythm on a strip.** One looped cell; then sixteen steps whose second half is made from the first, where on one line backwards and half-turn give the same loop; then a second voice, where they part and the loop reads as one of the seven frieze groups (kick-snare-kick-snare is p2mg, a glide); then the loop as a clock, where a 1/k turn is a slide of n/k steps. The test: five-fold in 16 steps leaves a gap or overlaps, as the section says, and in 15 or 20 steps it fits and plays. The bundle's recipes can be tried here: write the half, choose the fill. Checked in Node on the piece's own engine; the mix was not heard.

pieces.title: one tile · six steps
pieces.caption: **One tile, and only the operations change.** The tile alone; slid into p1; turned into p2, p3, p4, p6; reflected into pm, pg, cm; then the nine that combine, with their mirrors, glides and turn centres shown. The test: all seventeen from the one tile, turning together. Nothing is added but operations, as the section says. The kaleidoscope sentence holds in the five groups with no reflection; in the other twelve, half the copies turn the other way, and the pattern as a whole never turns.
